We have carbon NMR shifts list: 166.40, 131.87, 129.70, 129.70, 129.01, 129.01, 129.00, 52.24, 43.47, 38.60.

Carbonyl carbons typically appear around 160-220 ppm for C=O (esters, ketones, acids). Here we have a peak at 166.40 ppm, which likely corresponds to a carbonyl carbon (maybe an amide, ester, acid). Only one such high shift. Others are aromatic (~129) and aliphatic.

Thus number of carbonyl groups likely 1.

But could there be more carbonyls that are overlapping? Usually each carbonyl gives a distinct signal unless symmetry. Only one high shift. So answer 1.

We could also check IR for C=O stretch ~1700 cm-1, but we didn't get IR due to error. Could try again with correct call (no args).
